title: Foundations for Sustainable Contributor Success
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose

This page defines the operating model, tools, and commitments that underpin sustainable contributor success at Redwood. It brings together our working principles, role progression guidance, core benefits and eligibility checkpoints, hiring and onboarding expectations, and the internal tools matrix contributors need to do their best work.

Scope

Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors with >6 months expected tenure, and people managers across engineering, product, design, go-to-market, and core functions. This is a living document owned by People Ops with cross-functional contributors from Eng, Product, and Finance.

Principles (why this matters)

- Predictability: people should know the path and timelines for growth, role changes, and access to benefits.
- Transparency: criteria for promotion, reclassification, and benefits eligibility are explicit and reviewable.
- Early momentum: a structured first 90 days reduces time-to-impact and long-term churn.
- Sustainable workload: role design emphasizes focused responsibilities, measurable outcomes, and regular capacity checks.

Quick summary for managers

1. Complete role orientation checklist within first 10 business days.
2. Run a 30/60/90 career checkpoint with each new hire and record notes in the HR system.
3. Apply the role ladder criteria (see Role Progression Framework) when writing performance goals or promotion packets.

Role Progression Framework

Overview: Redwood uses a competency-and-impact model for role ladders. Each ladder is defined by three axes: technical/service mastery, scope of impact, and leadership/mentorship. Promotion decisions weigh these axes along with business needs.

Level bands (summary table)

| Band | Typical titles | Scope of impact | Expected outcomes (examples) |
|------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------------------|
| IC1  | Associate / Junior | Individual contributor, mentor-lite | Ship small features, reliable ops, learning focus |
| IC2  | Contributor | Feature ownership, cross-team delivery | Deliver subsystems, reliable QA/ops |
| IC3  | Senior | Multi-team influence, technical ownership | Lead major projects, mentor peers |
| IC4  | Staff / Principal | Strategic technical direction | Shape product/platform, coach leaders |
| M1   | Manager | Team-level delivery & growth | Recruit, set priorities, career coaching |
| M2   | Senior Manager | Multi-team ops | Program-level delivery, cross-functional leadership |

Detailed criteria: see related competency matrices (linked in related_pages) for role-specific examples (engineering, product, design, GTM).

Promotion & compensation cadence

- Formal promotion cycles: twice annually (May, November). Managers may submit off-cycle promotion packets for exceptional cases.
- Promotion packet contents: updated role profile, peer manager endorsements (2+), sample deliverables, manager assessment, and calibration notes.
- SLA: People Ops aims to communicate a promotion decision within 8 weeks of packet submission.

Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Objective: Get new contributors to a dependable, autonomous state as efficiently and sustainably as possible while ensuring psychological safety.

Pre-boarding (owner: Hiring manager + People Ops):
- Verify offer paperwork and access entitlements 5 business days before start.
- Share team README, roadmap summary, and first-week agenda.

Day 0–7 (owner: Manager + Buddy):
- Workspace & accounts: laptop, SSO access, Slack, GitHub, CI, ticketing, and time-tracking should be provisioned. Target: 95% provisioned by end of Day 1.
- Intro sessions: team sync, tech stack walkthrough, product overview, compliance & security briefing.

Day 8–30:
- First small ticket assigned (owner: manager): a scoped bugfix or documentation task with automated test and CI path.
- First 1:1 cadence established (weekly).

Day 30–90 (first 90-day plan):
- 30/60/90 checkpoints: explicit goals and success criteria recorded in the HR system.
- Impact goal by day 90: meaningful contribution to a team deliverable and at least one cross-team communication artifact (e.g., design doc).

Onboarding checklist (table)

| Item | Owner | Target | Verification |
|------|-------|--------|--------------|
| Laptop & VPN | IT | Day 0 | Ticket closed |
| SSO & GitHub | IT/Manager | Day 0 | Can clone repo |
| Security training | People Ops | Day 7 | Completion cert |
| Team runbook access | Manager | Day 3 | Access verified |
| First ticket merged | Manager | Day 30 | PR merged in main branch |

First 90-day template (manager guidance)

- 30-day: familiarity — setup complete, one small merged PR, product comprehension.
- 60-day: ownership — owning a feature area, regular contributions to team planning.
- 90-day: autonomy — leading a modest project, mentor pairing, and performance checkpoint.

Tools & Access Matrix

Redwood maintains a minimal required access set for new contributors. Managers request any additional privileges through the Access Request workflow.

| Resource | Default access | Escalation path |
|---------|----------------|-----------------|
| GitHub repos (team) | Write | Team lead approval |
| CI/CD (deploy) | Read | Release owner review |
| Production logs | Read-only (SAML group) | SRE + manager approval |
| Billing dashboard | None | Finance approval |

Sample access provisioning CLI (for admin teams)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# provision-basic-access.sh --username $1 --team $2
set -e
if [ -z "$1" ] || [ -z "$2" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <username> <team>"
  exit 1
fi
# Example calls to internal tooling (pseudo-CLI)
redwood-iam grant --user "$1" --group "team-$2"
redwood-ssm provision --user "$1" --role "contributor-basic"
redwood-git add-collaborator --repo "team-$2/core" --user "$1"

Benefits & Perks (high level)

- Health: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans; company pays 80% of employee premium cost.
- Financial: 401(k) with 4% match up to salary, biannual compensation review windows (May, Nov).
- Time off: 20 days PTO baseline (prorated year 1) plus 10 company holidays; flexible personal leave policy.
- Professional development: $2,500 annual learning stipend; sabbatical eligibility after 4 years.
- Wellbeing: mental health coverage, Employee Assistance Program, and quarterly wellbeing stipends.

Eligibility rules (examples):
- Full benefits begin on first day of employment for full-time employees.
- Contractors working >30 hours/week and engaged for >12 months: prorated benefits per contract terms.

Succession, Rotations, and Internal Mobility

- Short rotations: 3–6 month scoped rotations are encouraged; definition and approval by manager and receiving team required.
- Backfill plan: when a contributor rotates out, managers must publish a 30-day transition plan and identify a knowledge owner.
- Internal postings: all roles are posted internally for 3 business days before external posting unless business-critical.

Manager playbook for role transitions (numbered steps)

1. Discuss intent and timeline with the contributor and the receiving manager.
2. Create a role transition checklist with deliverables and knowledge transfer sessions.
3. Update team roadmap and capacity model.
4. Schedule overlap pairing for at least 10 business days for critical systems.

Measuring success (KPIs)

- New-hire ramp time: median time to first merged PR (target 21 days).
- Onboarding completion: % of new hires completing core checklist within 30 days (target 90%).
- Retention after one year for hires in the last 12 months (target >85%).
- Manager satisfaction with new hire readiness (quarterly survey target >4.0/5).

Common FAQs

Q: When is someone eligible for a promotion?
A: Eligibility requires 12 months in role except in exceptional impact cases. Use the role ladder matrices to prepare evidence.

Q: Who approves off-cycle hiring or promotions?
A: Hiring director + People Ops for headcount; Promotions off-cycle require manager justification and a director-level signoff.

Q: How do I request an internal rotation?
A: Talk to your manager, then file a Rotation Request in the HR portal. Expect a 10 business day review.
